notes.Mindseeker Oculus: The best common. A 3-drop that comes with a Jace on 4 loyalty.
notes.Extended Absence: Exiles a creature at instant speed. Black's best common.
notes.No Admittance: 3 damage to anything for 2 mana. Red's best common.
notes.Protege's Awakening: A card and a Jace on 6, and it often comes around pick 5.
notes.Surgical Precision: Kills a big creature, or draws when there is nothing to kill.
notes.Something Worth Saving: Card selection, graveyard fuel and a little life. Green's best common, and it goes late.

text: Fliers, Cadet tokens and life gain. Average commons and uncommons. Its best home by far is WU, the top pair; the other white pairs sit in the bottom half.

The deepest colour. Blue has the best commons in the set, more empower cards than any other colour, and three of the four best pairs: WU, UB and UR. It is light on creatures, so its decks win with fliers, card draw and Jace tokens.

Removal and graveyard creatures. Black has the most removal spells in the set, with red close behind. Its uncommons still average the lowest of any colour, so take the kill spells and let the rest come to you.
Burn, prowess and Heartwood. Red has the weakest commons, but the best card in the set is a red mythic and its removal is good. RG and UR are its strong pairs.

The weakest colour by its pairs' deck win rate. Green has no removal graded B or better and only two strong cards. It brings big creatures and ramp. Take it when it is clearly open, and pair it with red.

archetypes.name: Surveil fliers

text: Scry and surveil every turn, then attack with fliers that grow when you do. The best pair in the format by deck win rate. Good WU decks run the least removal of any pair (about four spells) and the most card draw, so the deck races in the air and bounces what it can't kill.

key: Prudent Fateseer
Pumps the team whenever you scry or surveil.
Desperate Futurescribe
A flier that puts a counter on a creature every turn you surveil.

archetypes.name: Graveyard control

text: Fill the graveyard, turn on threshold (seven or more cards in it) and win the long game with card draw and black removal. The second best pair. Good UB decks play fewer creatures than most, about thirteen or fourteen.

key: Recursive Recruitment
Two Cadets now, two bigger ones later from the graveyard.
Void Extrapolator
Mills three, then grows with threshold.

archetypes.name: Heartwood ramp

text: Make Heartwood tokens for mana, then land the biggest threats in the format a turn or two early. Good RG decks run the most mana sources and the most six-drops of any pair, and around seven removal spells.

key: Heartwood Crafter
A 1-drop whose spell makes a Heartwood token.
Craftwork Crusher
The top end the deck ramps into. Picks two of 4 damage, a Cadet and a card.

archetypes.name: Spells

text: Cheap instants and sorceries trigger prowess creatures and spell payoffs. Good UR decks play the fewest creatures of any pair, under thirteen, and the most evasion. The payoffs are thin, so most of the deck is just good blue and red spells.

key: Saheeli, Jewel of Avishkar
A hasty flying Thopter for every noncreature spell.
Clash of Elements
Instant-speed tuck. They choose: top of the library and 2 damage, or the bottom.

archetypes.name: Value creatures

text: Creatures that kill or draw something when they enter, backed by black removal. Good BG decks have plenty of both: around sixteen creatures and seven removal spells. The graveyard helps a little, but card quality matters more.

key: Primal Witchstalker
Menace, mills four and gets a land back.
Hapatra, the Desert Fang
Shrinks or kills a creature, scaled by your graveyard.

archetypes.name: Burn

text: Ping the opponent with damage outside combat, then cash in on cards that check for it. The payoffs are weak (none grades above C+), but the removal isn't: good BR decks run the most removal of any pair, about seven or eight spells.

key: Stingerquill Voxmancer
Pings the opponent for 1 on every turn it is prepared.
Grim Repriser
Comes back from the graveyard for 2 mana on a turn they took noncombat damage.

archetypes.name: Life gain

text: Gain a little life every turn and turn it into cards and counters. Good GW decks play the most creatures of any pair and have the least evasion, so they win on the ground. Below average by deck win rate.

key: Bloombrute
Draws a card the first time you gain life each turn.
Vigorbloom Vanguard
A 2-drop whose spell gives a counter and 1 life.

archetypes.name: Sacrifice

text: Trade creatures off and profit when they die. The death payoffs are weak, none grades above C+, so treat it as a removal deck with a small bonus. Good WB decks run about seven removal spells.

key: Twisted Fates
Destroys any nonland permanent. The best gold card in the pair.
Edgar, Ancient Bloodlord
Gains life when your creatures die and eats spare ones.

archetypes.name: Counters aggro

text: Put +1/+1 counters on cheap creatures and attack. Second worst by deck win rate. Its gold uncommons are below average, so draft it as plain aggro with good red and white cards and don't chase the theme.

key: Warrior's Blades
3 damage when it enters, then an equipment that is cheap to move onto creatures with counters.
Mabel, Valley Hero
Puts a counter on a creature whenever one of yours enters.

archetypes.name: Empower Jace

text: Build up a big Jace token and use Ways and other planeswalker cards to make it matter. The worst pair by deck win rate, even though blue is the deepest colour. Blue's empower cards are better spent in WU or UB unless green is clearly open.

key: Mind Meanderer
A 6-mana flier that fights when it enters.
Kiora of Salt and Sand
Gives planeswalkers an ability that makes an 8/8. Needs a big Jace.

text: Reality Fracture is a multiverse set built around planeswalkers. The ally pairs are the five colleges of Hexhaven, each with a Charm and its own plan. The enemy pairs each follow one planeswalker. Across every colour, empower cards put loyalty on a Jace token you control.
The numbers come from 17Lands Premier Draft data, 29 September to 8 November 2026. Deck counts and building figures are from players with a 60%+ win rate.

sections.heading: The format in short
list: Blue is the deepest colour. It has the best commons (mean GIH 56.4, the next colour 54.0) and plays in three of the four best pairs.
WU has the best deck win rate and GU the worst, even though both are blue. UB, RG and UR follow WU.
Rares decide a lot of games: 15 rares and mythics win at 62 or more, and no common reaches 60. Half of the bombs are planeswalkers.
Black and red have the most removal. Green has none graded B or better and is the weakest colour.
Play two colours. About one deck in seven among good players adds a third, and no three-colour combination beats the best pairs.
Every pair has a common dual land that enters untapped if you control a planeswalker. The Jace token counts.

text: Take power first. Bombs, rare planeswalkers and removal come before synergy. None of the pair themes showed a measurable edge in deck results, so the better card is usually right.

Read pack 1. What comes late in pack 1 says something about pack 3; pack 2 says very little. Top drafters ended in a pair their pack 1 neighbours left open about half the time (47%) and in a cut pair less than one time in five, but their results were the same either way.

Settle by the middle of pack 2. Strong drafters keep the pair they hold at ten cards about seven times in ten, and at fifteen cards about eight in ten. When they move, they change one colour. Changing both after the fifth card almost never happens.
Average counts from 30,683 decks of players with a 60%+ win rate. These describe a normal deck. Card quality is what makes it win.
Play enough removal. Decks with two removal spells or fewer win about three points less, and that holds for strong and weak players alike.

Sixteen lands is fine, and a little better than seventeen when the deck has two or more cheap card-flow spells: 2 mana or less, with draw, scry or surveil. Empower counts, since the Jace token surveils.
Within a pair, decks with a higher average mana value win slightly more. Don't cut good five- and six-drops to lower the curve.
A short creature count or few two-drops costs nothing measurable when the cards are good. Duals that enter tapped cost nothing measurable either, so play the ones in your colours.

pages.title: Empower Jace
pages.summary: Puts loyalty counters on your Jace token, making one first if you have none. The token can surveil 1 or draw a card.
pages.verdict: In every colour, most of all blue. A good empower card is a good card in any deck, and the Ways make it better.

text: The Jace token has two abilities: −1 to surveil 1 and −3 to draw a card. A big token is a card-advantage engine that also soaks up attacks. Several cards check whether you control a Jace or a planeswalker, including the common dual lands.

The Ways are uncommon enchantments that empower Jace by 2 to 7 and add a planeswalker bonus. In deck results, empower cards did about half a point per card better next to a Way and a third of a point worse without one. Read that as a lean, not a rule.
cards: The best common in the set.
A card and a Jace on 6.
Draws a card whenever you use a −2 or bigger ability.

pages.title: Prepared
pages.summary: Creatures with a spell attached. While the creature is prepared, you may cast a copy of the spell, which unprepares it.
pages.verdict: A small bonus in every colour, mostly on the college pairs' gold cards. Rate each card on its own.

text: Most prepared creatures enter prepared, so you get the spell once. A few become prepared again at the start of each of your turns and give you the spell every turn. Each college pair has three gold prepared creatures. As a group they win a little less often than an average card.

pages.title: Heartwood
pages.summary: A red and green artifact token that taps for red or green mana.
pages.verdict: RG only. The mana that lets RG cast its top end early.

text: Six cards make Heartwood tokens, five of them RG gold and one green rare. The tokens are artifacts, so cards that care about artifacts count them too.
The cards that win games on their own. Half of them are planeswalkers, and the red one is far ahead of the rest.
cards: The best card in the set by more than four points. Makes a Cadet on every loyalty ability, and −3 deals 4 to every creature except your tokens.
A 6-mana flier that recasts spells from your graveyard for free.
Draws a card on each of their turns and makes a blocker every turn.
Counter, bounce, copy and draw in one instant.
+2 shrinks a creature, −2 makes each player sacrifice one and leaves you a 4/4.
Makes 4/4 tramplers and draws when big creatures enter.
Random discard for X. Wins long games.
Exiles every creature and empowers Jace for each one.

text: Unconditional removal adds the most to a deck, damage-based removal about half as much, and removal that only hits some targets close to nothing. Counterspells count for a little over half a removal spell. Black and red have most of it; green has none graded B or better.
cards: An edict that takes their biggest creature or planeswalker.
6 damage, and the extra empowers Jace.
Sets a creature to 0/0 at instant speed. Counters on it still count.
Destroys a creature or planeswalker with mana value 3 or more.
6 damage and a counter on your creature.
Exiles any nonland permanent while it stays.
Destroys any creature. Kill an attacker and they draw nothing.
